answer.question: Do Westminster's artificial turf rules apply in Shaw Heights?
answer.answer: No. Shaw Heights is unincorporated and governed by Adams County, so Westminster's limits on where turf can go don't decide your layout. The county's rules exclude turf as a landscape material but are written for new development and changes of use.

blocks.h2: Westminster sends the water bill. Adams County writes the rules.
blocks.takeaway: A Westminster address and water bill don't make Westminster's turf limits yours; Adams County governs Shaw Heights. Give the county's Planner of the Day your address and ask whether the lot is unincorporated.
paras: Shaw Heights is an unincorporated community governed by Adams County, even though the Westminster post office, ZIP 80031, serves it (Wikipedia). Westminster's water rate sheets for 2025 and 2026 draw the same line, pricing In City at 1.0, Shaw Heights at 1.10 and Out of City at 1.25 (City of Westminster).

That matters when you read about turf in Westminster. The city's landscape regulations, adopted by its City Council, generally prohibit artificial turf except in detached and duplex yards away from streets, parks and open space (City of Westminster). Those limits shape our Westminster page, not a Shaw Heights layout.

Confirm the jurisdiction first, because a Westminster mailing address doesn't settle it. Adams County's Planner of the Day takes planning questions on 720.523.6800 or at cedd-plan@adamscountyco.gov (Adams County). Give the address and ask whether the lot is unincorporated.

blocks.h2: The county rules out turf in new development. An existing yard is a separate question.
blocks.takeaway: The county bars turf as landscape material in new development and changes of use, unless it accepts an alternative design. An existing house doesn't obviously fit either; ask whether your re-landscape needs review.
paras: Section 4-19-04-01 of the county's Development Standards and Regulations is direct: "No artificial trees, plants, or turf shall be used as a landscape material." An applicant who wants turf must still meet the plant minimums and ask the Director of Community and Economic Development to accept an alternative turf design with drainage specifications (Adams County DSR, Chapter 4).

Section 4-19-02 sets the reach of that rule: new development that had not applied for a building permit before the section took effect, and existing development that needs a change in use permit. The county says a change in use happens when "the essential character or nature of the activity conducted on a lot changes." A house that stays a house, with turf where the bluegrass was, doesn't obviously fit either.

That reading is not official. The county calls the Planner of the Day's advice general information; formal guidance takes a completed application, such as a zoning verification request through its ePermit Center (Adams County). Ask whether a re-landscape on an existing lot needs county review, front yard included, and bring the reply to the free visit so the layout fits it.

blocks.h2: The county's draft keeps the turf rule and adds a functional-use test.
blocks.takeaway: The draft code, starting 1 January 2027 if adopted, keeps the turf rule and adds a functional-use test. It doesn't name single-family yards; check the latest draft before relying on it.
paras: Adams County is replacing these regulations. Its project page sets the Planning Commission hearing for 22 October 2026 and the Board of County Commissioners hearing for 17 November 2026, with the new rules starting 1 January 2027 if adopted. Written comments on case PRC2026-00016 close on 2 October 2026 (Adams County).

The latest draft still bars artificial turf as a landscape material, and adds that an applicant must "demonstrate a functional use for the artificial turf." It says the landscaping division "generally applies to new construction" (Adams County draft, Chapter 4). Its outright ban on nonfunctional artificial turf covers new development and redevelopment on commercial, institutional and industrial property, common interest community property and rights-of-way, adding multifamily property of more than twelve units from 1 January 2028. A single-family yard isn't named. Our Colorado turf law guide covers the state law behind that list. Check the current draft before relying on it.

blocks.h2: Your lawn water is billed at Westminster's Shaw Heights rate.
blocks.takeaway: Shaw Heights pays more than city customers for water, and summer watering lands on those tiers alone. Turf takes the grass off them, though it still needs brushing and an occasional rinse.
paras: Westminster's 2026 single-family tiers for Shaw Heights are $4.62 per thousand gallons up to 8,000 gallons, $8.43 from 9,000 to 40,000 and $10.54 over 41,000, against $4.20, $7.66 and $9.58 in the city (City of Westminster). Sewer is charged on average winter use, so summer watering lands on the water tiers alone. If a different provider's name is on your bill, its rates and rules apply instead.

Westminster says three out of every four gallons a home uses in summer go on the lawn and garden. Its Drought Watch, in effect from 15 April 2026, asks for lawn watering on no more than three days a week, before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m., and its notice of 31 March said mandatory restrictions were not in place (City of Westminster). Ask the city for the current stage.

Turf takes the grass off those tiers. It still needs brushing, debris removal and a rinse now and then, and we walk you through that care when the work is done. Westminster's listed help runs from sprinkler audits to lawn replacement assistance and Garden in a Box discounts. Our guide to Denver-area rebates explains why lawn replacement money doesn't reach artificial turf.

blocks.h2: Smectitic clay on a 3 to 5 percent fall.
blocks.takeaway: Deeper down the clay reaches about 40%, and on a 3 to 5 percent fall it can wet and move unevenly. We measure the fall and build a compacted base to hold the low side.
paras: USDA soil data at the centre of Shaw Heights maps Platner loam, 3 to 5 percent slopes. Platner is 85% of that map unit, a well-drained soil classed as fine and smectitic, with Wages and Stoneham soils making up the rest (USDA Soil Data Access). Its surface layer is about 19% clay. Deeper down the clay reaches about 40%, and USDA's linear extensibility figure, its shrink-swell measure, peaks at 7.3%.

On a lot with a fall, that combination sets the job. Sprinkler and storm water run downhill before they soak in, and clay that wets unevenly moves unevenly. We measure the fall at the free visit, then take out the old lawn, prepare the subgrade and build a compacted base for this soil, with the turf laid, seamed and edged so the low side holds its line.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Shaw Heights, CO?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Shaw Heights, CO. Westminster supplies the water and bills Shaw Heights at a rate of its own, but Adams County governs the lot, so the county's rules are the ones to check before a layout is final. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Can turf go in a Shaw Heights front yard?
faq.a: Westminster's limit doesn't decide it, but that isn't a yes. The county's landscaping section excludes artificial turf as a landscape material for new development and changes of use (Adams County DSR, Chapter 4), and nothing we found speaks to an existing front yard directly. Get the county's answer for your lot before we draw one.

faq.q: Does my HOA still get a say?
faq.a: If your street has an HOA, yes. Its approval is separate from the county's, so get both before you commit to a shape. Colorado law limits what an HOA can refuse in the back yard of a detached home, and our Colorado HOA turf guide explains how far that goes.

faq.q: Do I need a county permit for a retaining wall or regrading?
faq.a: Ask before the layout is final. Adams County adopted the 2024 editions of the International Codes, in effect from 1 July 2026, and its Permits & Licensing division answers questions on 720-523-6800 (Adams County). We measure the fall at the free visit, so you know whether the layout calls for a wall or a grade change before you ask.
